topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, speaker introduction, and learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Genetic, intrinsic, and environmental contributions to cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer by exploring the interplay between intrinsic cellular errors, genetic predisposition, and environmental risk factors supported by epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how viral, bacterial, and parasitic pathogens drive oncogenesis, using the multi-step pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation and induce DNA damage through adduct formation and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and physiological susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain non-mutagenic tumour promotion mechanisms and demonstrate how tissue inflammation, signaling activation, and developmental timing contribute to malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity and assess human cancer risk.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing summary and final takeaways of the lecture.
